units.text: INT. PAROLE OFFICE - DAY
ON CAMERA: handheld, slightly too close, a fluorescent hum.
A wall of grey filing cabinets.
THE WOMAN, 30s, sits across from a desk, hands flat on her knees, avoiding the lens.
KIM, 50s, parole officer, reads a folder.
Beside her a plastic nameplate reads KIP DAVIS, PO II.
Kim is not Kip.
Kip is the one leaning in the doorway, eating a bagel.
Camera stays off the client please. We agreed.
units.name: KIM

units.text: Its a documentary Kim. Everybody signed.
units.name: KIP

units.text: Not her.
units.name: KIM

units.text: I signed.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: You signed a form that said "a person". You didn't know it'd be this.
units.name: KIM

units.text: I didn't know a lot of things when I signed stuff.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Eleven months clean, curfew met, job at the laundromat, check ins on time. Honestly Jen you're the best file I've got this quarter and I've been dreading this meeting all week.
units.name: KIM

units.text: Jen. There it is. Finally a name.
units.name: KIP

units.text: Dreading why?
units.name: JEN

units.text: Because your sponsor called me. Because he said he wants to put his name on your housing form. As your partner.
units.name: KIM

units.text: Mo.
units.name: JEN

units.text: Mo Haddad. Who has a record. Who's two years out himself. Associating with known offenders is a violation, you know that, I know that, Kip knows that.
units.name: KIM

units.text: I know that.
units.name: KIP

units.text: So violate me.
units.name: JEN

units.text: Don't make this a joke.
units.name: KIM

units.text: I'm not joking. I love him. I've never said that out loud in this building. It's the first thing I've said in here that wasn't a lie or an excuse.
units.name: JEN

units.text: Silence.
Kim closes the folder.
The camera shakes, someone has stopped breathing behind it.
Sign here. And here. I never saw the second page.
units.name: KIM

units.text: Neither did the camera.
units.name: KIP
